notes.account: A wholly handwritten working sheet, with formulas (5) through the final 17/12-uncertain label and the heading 1.2. Deux décompositions binaires. A pencil 32 is at the bottom-left edge and is retained as archive numbering. No separate author page number, date, author-written question mark, or explicit proof-check annotation is visible. No drawing or arrow diagram occurs.

The opening words are Notons les implications. In display (5), the upper line places a rightward double arrow after X connexe; the lower line has a double-headed double arrow between X connexe and the E/empty-set comparison. The older capital and relation strokes, uncertain state of Si, and detached left-hand mark are retained. The visible final comparison signs are crossed not-equal signs; the empty sets are slashed ovals.

Display (6) introduces the raised ring-epsilon Sigma notation and writes a chain of differences and intersections. The parenthesis has omega followed by a membership/not-equal/equality-uncertain joined sign. The round two-lobe omega in (7) supported the recurring letter reading; the clean equality in (7) did not settle the different relation stroke in (6).

Display (7) has three union terms and a right-hand two-entry parenthesis. Corrections affect an older mark before the first epsilon and low suffixes at four locations. Both entries of the right-hand parenthesis visibly have high primes, while the first term of the union has an unprimed live epsilon. This written discrepancy remains. H explicit note about corrected indices and parenthetical primes was read and used as editorial context, without treating the note itself as ink.

Display (8) has three long overbars above Sigma together with its raised group, then a final Sigma with a separate dot above it and a small comma inside the raised ring-comma-epsilon group. The terminal low-right mark remains uncertain. No operation name was inferred from the notation.

The abandoned lines read “On a le cas” and “on s’intéresse à la cond”, each crossed by a continuous rising cancellation stroke. The earlier sentence retains the readable cancelled word “trois”. No completion of either abandoned phrase was supplied.

Section 1.2 defines the written phrase non parallèles, with underline under parallèles and an interlinear clause “si elles sont distinctes, et”. Display (10) shows an intersection followed by equality and an empty-set glyph. The subsequent displays show the written inclusions Sigma_1^+ subset Sigma_2^- and Sigma_2^+ subset Sigma_1^-. The intervening prose is copied as “condition qui équivaut :” and “ou encore :”. This is a source account, not a proof of the displayed relationship.

The last line writes two negative-Sigma names and the word definis without a detached acute. The final display lists two pairs, but its final low index remains 1/2-uncertain and its label remains 17/12-uncertain. The symmetry of the preceding pairs and the sequence of formula numbers were considered only as reading cues and were not used to replace these observed glyphs.

All mathematical material was read for transcription and local glyph comparison. No targeted proof check, independent re-proof, computation, formal certificate or background-theorem recheck was performed. check_events is therefore empty.
